text: There's something you started, and never finished.
And part of your mind is still working on it. Right now.
In the 1920s, in a Berlin café, a psychologist noticed something strange about a waiter.
He never wrote anything down. He remembered every open order. Perfectly.
But the moment a bill was paid, it was gone.
His student, Bluma Zeigarnik, took it into the lab.
She gave people simple tasks, and interrupted half of them.
Later, they remembered the unfinished ones almost twice as well.
An open loop keeps running. In the background.
That's the idea you keep almost starting. The message you never sent. The thing you'll do someday.
Every one of them is an open tab in your head.
But here's the part nobody tells you.
You don't have to finish it to close it.
Researchers found that just making a specific plan quiets the loop.
Your brain doesn't need it done. It needs it decided.
So pick one. Write down exactly when.
Or start it for two minutes. Tonight.
Because you're carrying all of them either way.
So which one is still running?
